newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-EL GERROUJ FAILS TO BREAK MORCELI'S RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-EL GERROUJ FAILS TO BREAK MORCELI'S RECORD.

text.p: World indoor champion Hicham El Guerrouj of Morroco failed in his attempt to break Algerian Noureddine Morceli's 1500 metres world record on a rainy night on Monday.

El Guerrouj, who had said he would go for Morceli's best mark of three minutes 27.37 seconds set two years ago, won his race easily in an international meeting in this Paris suburb but could manage only a relatively modest time of 3:31.76.

"The conditions were not ideal and the pace in he first 500 metres was too slow," said El Guerrouj, who clocked a world class time of 3:29.51 last Saturday in the Dutch city of Hengelo. "Never mind, I'll try again."
American Bryan Robson had earlier run the fastest men's 400 metres hurdles so far this year with a winning time of 48.24 seconds.
Compatriot Derrick Adkins, the world and Olympic champion, fell before the last hurdle but he was not hurt.

American world champion Kim Batten, wearing her trademark sunglasses despite the miserable weather, won the women's 400 metres hurdles race in 53.63 seconds ahead of arch rival Deon Hemmings of Jamaica, the Olympic champion, who was second in 54.02.

"I didn't feel particularly good but it wasn't a bad race," said Batten after clocking the best time this year. "It's only my fourth meeting this season and there are still quite a few things I must work on", she added.
